🏡 Village

Short-notice kid care from SOM classmates you trust

Saachi Wadhwani · MGT 409 · Fall 2026
github.com/saachiwadhwani-yale/village
Demo video (the real Slack version): Google Drive · Local testing: a Slack-like web demo

The problem

  • Student parents' days are full of short, fixed blocks: an 80-minute class, a coffee chat
  • When childcare falls through, it's skip it or bring the kid
  • Classmates would help, but finding one who's free means texting people one by one and waiting
  • A sitter averages $21/hour (Care.com 2025) and isn't built for 40 minutes on short notice
  • From an SOM parent interview: trust is set once (a small approved group), class time is a real need, and helpers should cancel a day ahead if they can

What's new

  • A village: classmates the parent approved once, ahead of time
  • Asks only people who are actually free: reads all their calendars (busy times only) or what they wrote
  • A dispatch agent runs the search: spins up an availability agent per classmate (rules first, close calls judged), then decides how many to ask: more, sooner, when it's last-minute or several kids
  • The first yes books it, never twice; with 2+ kids, Village also finds a second helper
  • Helper can't make it? Village quietly finds cover before the parent is bothered
  • Lives in Slack, where SOM already is

gpt-6-luna: $0.10 / 1M in, $0.50 / 1M out. The rules tool settles clear cases in two short calls; low reasoning effort stopped occasional 3,000-token overthinking. Hosting (~$12/month) costs about as much as the model at 10,000 users.

Safety

  • Classmates' text is untrusted data; agents that read it can't act (no tools, or read-only ones)
  • The availability agent can't overrule the rules (code checks it)
  • Kid's allergies and notes go only to the helper, after they say yes
  • First yes wins in one DB update; no double booking, even across villages
  • Agents see busy times, never event names

Impact

  • 4.8 million US college students are raising children (IWPR)
  • Setup: about 3 minutes, once (shown in the demo video)
  • Asking: one message and one tap; classmates are asked ~15 seconds later, with everyone's calendars already checked
  • Village keeps asking more people until someone says yes, so the parent just waits
  • Only classmates who look free are asked, so busy people aren't bothered

Limits and next steps

  • Runs on a laptop today
  • Calendar feeds can lag by hours; direct integration would fix it
  • Close calls can vary run to run
  • No user study yet
  • Host it; work with IT on an SOM-wide workspace
  • Recurring requests (weekly class)
  • WhatsApp, where many SOM parents already coordinate
